selection_rules: gross list of 4,631 unique government contracts from the Mercell outsourcing database 2004-2014
exclude contracts with a start date before 2004 or after 2014 (to allow register matching and at least three post-outsourcing years)

exclude contracts below the EU threshold limits, contracts without information on the winning vendor, contracts for products and construction projects, and contracts offered by international organizations or public utility companies

manually remove purchases outside the four service areas (cleaning, road and park maintenance, retirement homes, canteen and catering), purchases of products, and contracts explicitly stating that no job changes were involved, leaving 691 cases

treated individuals: employed by the relevant government agency in T-1, not employed by the private vendor in T-1, employed by the private vendor in T0

include only individuals shifting in the year with most job transfers, if within one year of the year in the official contract documents, and only where that year's transfers exceed the second-largest year, are at least twice the average across all years, and at least three times the third-largest year
result: 73 instances of government outsourcing and 1,478 treated individuals over 2005-2013
control group: exclude individuals who received treatment in any year; exclude individuals who did not work in the public sector in T-1 and who did not have at least one workplace in T0 and T-1
exact matching (CEM) on job function (DISCO code) in T-1 and treatment year; only job-function-by-year strata with at least one treatment and one control observation are included

claims.statement: Government outsourcing reduces the annual work income of transferred employees one year after outsourcing relative to matched public employees who were not outsourced.

treatment.label: Government outsourcing (employee transferred from government employment to the third-party vendor receiving the outsourcing contract)

register_source.value: Not a single named register variable: built by merging 218 winning-vendor CVR numbers from the Official Danish Company Register (CVR register) with Statistics Denmark individual-level employment registers for all public employees 2003-2015

definition.value: Binary indicator for being one of the 1,478 individuals who (i) was employed by the outsourcing government agency in the year before outsourcing (T-1), (ii) was not employed by the private vendor in T-1, and (iii) was employed by the private vendor in T0; further restricted to individuals shifting in the year with most job transfers for that contract, within one year of the contract date, and only where that year's transfers exceed the second-largest year, are at least twice the yearly average and at least three times the third-largest year. key_assumptions.supported_by: Stated construction of the matched sample; DISCO contains more than 1200 job groups in the gross sample

key_assumptions.assumption: The coded job changes are caused by outsourcing rather than by voluntary mobility (treatment is measured without systematic error)
key_assumptions.supported_by: Transfer-count rules (largest transfer year, within one year of the contract date, exceeding twice the average and three times the third-largest year) and a robustness check varying the cut-offs

key_assumptions.supported_by: The authors state that the data are observational and encourage future research to look for natural experiments; no specific unobserved confounder is named
